# toolbelt commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-skill.ts from the CLI's registry (toolbelt 1.0.0). Do not edit. -->

Run every command as `node <skill-dir>/scripts/toolbelt.mjs <command> ...`. Input: an argument,
`--file <path>`, or stdin. Every command also takes `--json` (structured output), `--file`/`-f`,
`--out`/`-o <path>` (write the output to a file), `--lang en|fr|de` and `--help`.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 invalid input (message on stderr), 2 wrong usage (unknown option, missing input).

123 tools run offline in the CLI; 16 are browser-only (their command prints the link).

- **Toolbelt**: `help`, `list`, `search`, `info`, `link`, `version`
- **Text**: `counter`, `diff`, `case`, `ascii-art`, `cipher`, `columns`, `emoji`, `escape`, `extract`, `html-to-markdown`, `lines`, `list-compare`, `lorem`, `markdown`, `morse`, `nato`, `numeronym`, `readability`, `regex`, `replace`, `slugify`, `speech` (browser), `unicode`, `whitespace`, `wrap`
- **Encoding & crypto**: `base64`, `base-encodings`, `url-encode`, `url-parser`, `html-entities`, `jwt`, `hash`, `hmac`, `password-hash`, `uuid`, `password`, `totp`, `keypair`, `qr`, `data-uri`, `encrypt`, `compress`, `certificate`, `basic-auth`, `bip39`, `safelink`
- **Data & formats**: `json`, `convert`, `csv`, `markdown-table`, `json-to-ts`, `json-diff`, `jsonpath`, `sql`, `xml`, `env`, `query-string`, `json-to-code`, `json-schema`, `html-to-jsx`, `json-tree`, `json-xml`, `docker-compose`
- **Time & numbers**: `timestamp`, `timezones`, `date-calc`, `cron`, `number-base`, `bytes`, `roman`, `number-words`, `percentage`, `units`, `aspect-ratio`
- **Web & dev**: `color`, `css-units`, `chmod`, `cidr`, `semver`, `user-agent`, `http-status`, `mime`, `ascii`, `gitignore`, `commit`, `validators`, `meta-tags`, `ip-tools`, `mac-address`, `ipv6-ula`, `random-port`, `git-cheatsheet`, `email-normalize`, `http-headers`, `curl-convert`
- **CSS & design**: `box-shadow`, `gradient`, `border-radius`, `cubic-bezier`, `clip-path`, `glassmorphism`, `css-triangle`, `svg-placeholder`, `type-scale`, `palette`

## Toolbelt

### help

Show every command, or one command's usage, options and examples.

```
toolbelt help [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt help
toolbelt help diff
```

### list

List the tools (id, category, whether the CLI runs it, title).

```
toolbelt list [--category <id>] [--json]
```

- `-c, --category <text|encode|data|convert|web|design|image|calc|life>`: Only this category.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt list
toolbelt list --category encode --json   # Encoding tools, as JSON.
```

### search

Find tools by words (titles, descriptions and keywords in English, French and German).

```
toolbelt search <words>
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt search json yaml
toolbelt search mot de passe
```

### info

A tool's title, description, URL, whether the CLI runs it, and its share-link keys.

```
toolbelt info <tool>
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt info jwt
toolbelt info tuner --json
```

### link

A link to a tool on the site with its input prefilled (the state is in the #fragment, never sent).

```
toolbelt link <tool> [--set key=value ...] [--set-file key=path ...] [--state '<json>']
```

- `-s, --set <key=value>`: Set one state key (repeatable).
- `--set-file <key=path>`: Set one state key to a file's content (repeatable).
- `--state <json>`: Several keys at once, as a JSON object.

Values are typed after each key's default (numbers, true/false, JSON for arrays and objects). `toolbelt info <tool>` lists a tool's keys; references/commands.md lists them all.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt link json --set input='{"a":1}' --set indent=4
toolbelt link diff --set-file a=old.txt --set-file b=new.txt
toolbelt link color --set color='#ff6600'
```

### version

Print the toolbelt version.

```
toolbelt version
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt version
```

## Text

### counter

Count characters, words, lines, sentences, bytes, tokens and reading time.

Aliases: `count`, `wc`.

```
toolbelt counter [text] [--top <n>] [--min-length <n>]
```

- `--top <n>`: Also list the n most frequent words. Default: 0.
- `--min-length <n>`: Ignore words shorter than this in --top. Default: 1.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt counter "Hello world. How are you?"
toolbelt counter --file README.md --top 10 --min-length 4 --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/counter

### diff

Compare two texts or files: unified patch, line summary, or word/character diff.

```
toolbelt diff <old-file> <new-file> [--format unified|lines|words|chars|summary] [--a <text>] [--b <text>]
```

- `--format <unified|lines|words|chars|summary>`: Output: a unified patch, changed lines (- / +), an inline word or character diff ([-old-]{+new+}), or counts. Default: unified.
- `--a <text>`: The old text, inline (instead of a file).
- `--b <text>`: The new text, inline (instead of a file).
- `-U, --context <n>`: Context lines in the patch. Default: 3.
- `-w, --ignore-whitespace`: Ignore whitespace changes.
- `-i, --ignore-case`: Ignore case.
- `--exit-code`: Exit with 1 when the inputs differ (like diff/git diff).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt diff old.txt new.txt   # A unified patch (git apply compatible).
toolbelt diff --a "the quick fox" --b "the slow fox" --format words
toolbelt diff a.json b.json --format summary --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/diff

### case

Convert case: camel, pascal, snake, kebab, constant, dot, path, train, title, sentence, lower, upper.

```
toolbelt case [text] [--to <case>]
```

- `-t, --to <case>`: The case to convert to (without it: every case).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt case "XMLHttpRequest handler" --to snake
toolbelt case "hello world"   # Every case at once.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/case

### ascii-art

Draw text as a FIGlet ASCII-art banner, optionally in a box frame.

Aliases: `figlet`.

```
toolbelt ascii-art [text] [--font <font>] [--width <n>] [--align left|center|right] [--frame] [--style <style>]
```

- `--font <standard|small|big|slant|banner3>`: FIGlet font. Default: standard.
- `--layout <font|full|fit|smush>`: Letter spacing: the font's own, full width, fitted, or smushed. Default: font.
- `--width <n>`: Wrap at this many columns (0: no wrap). Default: 80.
- `--align <left|center|right>`: Alignment of the lines. Default: left.
- `--no-banner`: Keep the text as is (only frame it).
- `--frame`: Draw a box around the result.
- `--style <single|double|rounded|heavy|ascii|stars|hash>`: Frame style. Default: single.
- `--pad-x <n>`: Spaces left and right inside the frame. Default: 1.
- `--pad-y <n>`: Empty lines above and below inside the frame. Default: 0.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt ascii-art "Hello"
toolbelt ascii-art "Deploy done" --font small --frame --style rounded
toolbelt ascii-art "Note" --no-banner --frame --style double
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/ascii-art

### cipher

ROT13, ROT47, Caesar and Atbash ciphers, with a Caesar brute force.

Aliases: `rot13`.

```
toolbelt cipher [text] [--cipher rot13|rot47|caesar|atbash] [--shift <n>] [--decode] [--brute-force]
```

- `-c, --cipher <rot13|rot47|caesar|atbash>`: The cipher. Default: rot13.
- `--shift <n>`: Caesar shift. Default: 3.
- `-d, --decode`: Decode instead of encode.
- `--brute-force`: Try the 25 Caesar shifts, the most readable first.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt cipher "Hello"   # ROT13: Uryyb.
toolbelt cipher "Khoor" --cipher caesar --shift 3 --decode
toolbelt cipher "Wkh fdw vdw" --brute-force
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/cipher

### columns

Extract or reorder columns of delimited text (CSV, TSV, pipes, spaces).

Aliases: `cut`.

```
toolbelt columns [text] [--columns <spec>] [--delimiter auto|comma|tab|semicolon|pipe|spaces|<chars>] [--out-delimiter <d>]
```

- `-c, --columns <spec>`: Columns to keep, 1-based, in order: "1,3", "2-4", "3-" , "4-1" (reversed). Default: all.
- `-d, --delimiter <d>`: Input delimiter: auto, comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, spaces, or any characters. Default: auto.
- `--out-delimiter <d>`: Output delimiter: same, comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, space, or any characters. Default: same.
- `--no-quotes`: Treat " as a plain character.
- `--no-trim`: Keep spaces around fields.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt columns --file data.csv --columns 1,3   # Columns 1 and 3.
ps aux | toolbelt columns --delimiter spaces --columns 2,11-
toolbelt columns --file data.tsv --columns 3-1 --out-delimiter comma
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/columns

### emoji

Search emojis by name or keyword (English, French, German), with code points.

```
toolbelt emoji <words> [--tone 0-5] [--limit <n>] [--group <group>]
```

- `--tone <n>`: Skin tone: 0 default, 1 light … 5 dark. Default: 0.
- `-n, --limit <n>`: At most this many results. Default: 20.
- `-g, --group <smileys|people|animals|food|travel|activities|objects|symbols|flags>`: Only this group (alone: list the group).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt emoji rocket
toolbelt emoji thumbs up --tone 3 --limit 1
toolbelt emoji --group flags --limit 300 --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/emoji

### escape

Escape or unescape a string for JSON, JavaScript, HTML, XML, SQL, CSV, regex or shell.

```
toolbelt escape [text] [--format <format>] [--unescape] [--ascii]
```

- `-t, --format <json|js|html|xml|sql|csv|regex|shell>`: The syntax to escape for. Default: json.
- `-u, --unescape`: Unescape instead of escape.
- `--ascii`: js/html/xml: escape every non-ASCII character too.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt escape 'He said "hi"' --format json
toolbelt escape "it's" --format shell
toolbelt escape '&lt;b&gt;' --format html --unescape
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/escape

### extract

Extract emails, URLs, domains, IPs, phone numbers, hashtags, mentions, numbers, dates, colors, card numbers.

```
toolbelt extract [text] [--kind <kind> ...] [--sort] [--no-dedupe] [--csv]
```

- `-k, --kind <email|url|domain|ipv4|ipv6|phone|hashtag|mention|number|date|color|card>`: What to extract (repeatable). Default: everything.
- `--sort`: Sort each list.
- `--no-dedupe`: Keep duplicates.
- `--csv`: Output CSV (kind,value).

Exits with 1 when nothing is found.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt extract --file page.html --kind email
toolbelt extract --file log.txt --kind ipv4 --kind url --sort --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/extract

### html-to-markdown

Convert HTML to Markdown (GitHub tables, strikethrough and task lists included).

Aliases: `html2md`.

```
toolbelt html-to-markdown [html] [--heading atx|setext] [--bullet -|*|+] [--code backticks|tildes|indented] [--no-gfm]
```

- `--heading <atx|setext>`: Heading style (# or underlined). Default: atx.
- `--bullet <-|*|+>`: List bullet. Default: -.
- `--code <backticks|tildes|indented>`: Code block style. Default: backticks.
- `--em <_|*>`: Emphasis delimiter. Default: _.
- `--links <inlined|referenced>`: Inline links or reference links at the end. Default: inlined.
- `--no-gfm`: Plain Markdown (no tables, strikethrough, task lists).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt html-to-markdown '<h1>Title</h1><p>Some <b>bold</b> text</p>'
toolbelt html-to-markdown --file page.html --out page.md
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/html-to-markdown

### lines

Sort, dedupe, trim, reverse, shuffle, number, prefix or suffix lines.

```
toolbelt lines [text] [--sort az|za|natural|length] [--dedupe] [--trim] [--remove-empty] [--reverse] [--shuffle] [--number]
```

- `--trim`: Trim spaces around each line.
- `--remove-empty`: Remove empty lines.
- `-u, --dedupe`: Remove duplicate lines (first kept).
- `-s, --sort <none|az|za|natural|length>`: Sort order. Default: none.
- `-i, --ignore-case`: Dedupe ignoring case.
- `--case-sensitive`: Sort with case (default: ignore case).
- `-r, --reverse`: Reverse the order.
- `--shuffle`: Shuffle (seeded).
- `--seed <n>`: Shuffle seed. Default: 1.
- `-n, --number`: Number the lines.
- `--number-start <n>`: First number. Default: 1.
- `--number-sep <text>`: Text after the number. Default: ". ".
- `--prefix <text>`: Add before each line.
- `--suffix <text>`: Add after each line.

Steps run in a fixed order: trim, remove empty, dedupe, sort, reverse, shuffle, number, prefix/suffix.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt lines --file names.txt --sort natural --dedupe
toolbelt lines --file list.txt --trim --remove-empty --number
toolbelt lines --file ids.txt --prefix "'" --suffix "',"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/lines

### list-compare

Compare two lists: items only in A, only in B, in both, and the union.

```
toolbelt list-compare <file-a> <file-b> [--a <text>] [--b <text>] [--show <part>] [--ignore-case]
```

- `--a <text>`: List A inline (one item per line).
- `--b <text>`: List B inline.
- `--show <all|only-a|only-b|both|union>`: Which result to print. Default: all.
- `-i, --ignore-case`: Compare ignoring case.
- `--commas`: Also split items on commas and semicolons.
- `--no-trim`: Keep spaces around items.
- `--sort`: Sort the results.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt list-compare before.txt after.txt
toolbelt list-compare --a $'a\nb\nc' --b $'b\nc\nd' --show only-a
toolbelt list-compare --a "x, y" --b "y, z" --commas --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/list-compare

### lorem

Generate lorem ipsum placeholder text (paragraphs, sentences or words; seeded).

Aliases: `lipsum`.

```
toolbelt lorem [count] [--unit paragraphs|sentences|words] [--html] [--seed <n>]
```

- `--unit <paragraphs|sentences|words>`: What to count. Default: paragraphs.
- `-n, --count <n>`: How many (also as the argument). Default: 3.
- `--html`: Wrap paragraphs in <p>.
- `--no-lorem`: Do not start with "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet".
- `--seed <n>`: Random seed (same seed, same text). Default: 1.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt lorem
toolbelt lorem 50 --unit words
toolbelt lorem 2 --html --seed 7
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/lorem

### markdown

Render Markdown to HTML, or list its headings / table of contents.

Aliases: `md`.

```
toolbelt markdown [text] [--toc] [--headings] [--no-gfm] [--breaks]
```

- `--toc`: Print a Markdown table of contents instead.
- `--headings`: List the headings (depth, text, anchor slug).
- `--no-gfm`: Plain CommonMark (no GitHub tables, task lists…).
- `--breaks`: Single line breaks become <br>.

The HTML is not sanitized (the site sanitizes it in the browser): do not serve untrusted input as is.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt markdown --file README.md --out README.html
toolbelt markdown --file README.md --toc
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/markdown

### morse

Translate text to Morse code and back (direction detected automatically).

```
toolbelt morse [text] [--mode auto|encode|decode]
```

- `-m, --mode <auto|encode|decode>`: Direction (auto: Morse input is decoded). Default: auto.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt morse "SOS"   # ... --- ...
toolbelt morse "... --- ..."   # SOS
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/morse

### nato

Spell text with a spelling alphabet (NATO, French, German DIN 5009).

Aliases: `spell`.

```
toolbelt nato [text] [--alphabet nato|fr|de|deNames] [--mark-case] [--table]
```

- `-a, --alphabet <nato|fr|de|deNames>`: Spelling alphabet (default: nato, or the --lang one).
- `--mark-case`: Mark upper and lower case letters.
- `--table`: Print the whole alphabet.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt nato "AB12"   # Alfa Bravo One Two
toolbelt nato --table --alphabet de
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/nato

### numeronym

Make numeronyms (internationalization → i18n), or expand known ones (a11y, k8s…).

```
toolbelt numeronym [text] [--min-length <n>] [--lowercase] [--expand]
```

- `--min-length <n>`: Leave shorter words as they are. Default: 4.
- `--lowercase`: Lowercase the result.
- `-x, --expand`: Look up the numeronyms in the text instead.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt numeronym "internationalization localization"   # i18n l10n
toolbelt numeronym "a11y and k8s" --expand
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/numeronym

### readability

Readability scores (Flesch, Flesch-Kincaid, Fog, SMOG, Coleman-Liau, ARI, LIX…) in English, French or German.

```
toolbelt readability [text] [--language auto|en|fr|de] [--long-from <words>]
```

- `--language <auto|en|fr|de>`: The text's language (auto-detected by default). Default: auto.
- `--long-from <n>`: Count sentences of at least this many words as long. Default: 25.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt readability --file article.md
toolbelt readability --file texte.txt --language fr --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/readability

### regex

Test a regular expression (JavaScript syntax) against a text: matches, positions and groups.

```
toolbelt regex <pattern> [text] [--flags gimsu]
```

- `--flags <flags>`: Any of g, i, m, s, u. Default: g.
- `-p, --pattern <regex>`: The pattern (then the argument is the text).

The text is the rest of the arguments, else --file, else stdin. Exits with 1 when nothing matches.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt regex '\d+' 'order 66 and 42'
toolbelt regex '(?<user>\w+)@(?<host>[\w.]+)' --file emails.txt --json
toolbelt regex '^error' --flags gim --file app.log
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/regex

### replace

Find and replace in a text, plain or with a regular expression ($1, $<name> in the replacement).

```
toolbelt replace [text] --find <s> --with <s> [--regex] [--flags gimsu] [--whole-word] [--escapes]
```

- `--find <text>`: What to find (required).
- `-w, --with <text>`: The replacement (default: empty). Default: "".
- `-r, --regex`: --find is a regular expression.
- `--flags <flags>`: Any of g, i, m, s, u. Default: g.
- `--whole-word`: Plain mode: whole words only.
- `--escapes`: Read \n, \t, \r and \\ in --find and --with.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt replace --file notes.txt --find foo --with bar
toolbelt replace '2024-05-01' --regex --find '(\d+)-(\d+)-(\d+)' --with '$3/$2/$1'
toolbelt replace --file list.txt --find ', ' --with '\n' --escapes
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/replace

### slugify

Turn text into a URL slug (one per line): accents removed, lowercase, dashes.

Aliases: `slug`.

```
toolbelt slugify [text] [--separator <s>] [--keep-case] [--max-length <n>] [--keep-unicode] [--umlauts]
```

- `-s, --separator <s>`: Word separator. Default: -.
- `--keep-case`: Do not lowercase.
- `--max-length <n>`: Cut at a word boundary (0: no limit). Default: 0.
- `--keep-unicode`: Keep letters with no ASCII form (Cyrillic, CJK…).
- `--umlauts`: ä → ae, ö → oe, ü → ue (default with --lang de).
- `--no-umlauts`: ä → a even with --lang de.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt slugify "Héllo Wörld: a guide!"   # hello-world-a-guide
toolbelt slugify "Grüße aus Köln" --umlauts --separator _
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/slugify

### speech (browser only)

Read text aloud with the system's voices. Needs the browser's speech synthesis (Web Speech API).

```
toolbelt speech
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt speech
toolbelt link speech --set text="Hello there"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/speech

### unicode

Inspect every code point (name, category, script, UTF-8/UTF-16), find invisible characters, normalize.

```
toolbelt unicode [text] [--normalize NFC|NFD|NFKC|NFKD] [--remove-invisible] [--normalize-spaces] [--limit <n>]
```

- `--normalize <NFC|NFD|NFKC|NFKD>`: Print the text in this normalization form.
- `--remove-invisible`: Print the text without zero-width, bidi and other invisible characters.
- `--normalize-spaces`: Print the text with unusual spaces made plain.
- `-n, --limit <n>`: At most this many code points in the table. Default: 500.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt unicode 'café ☕'
toolbelt unicode --file suspicious.txt --remove-invisible --out clean.txt
toolbelt unicode 'é' --normalize NFD --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/unicode

### whitespace

Clean text: invisible characters, odd spaces, trailing spaces, blank lines, tabs, quotes, dashes, accents…

Aliases: `clean`.

```
toolbelt whitespace [text] [--blank-lines keep|collapse|remove] [--quotes straight|smart|german] [--inspect] [...]
```

- `--inspect`: Only report what the text contains (no cleaning).
- `--keep-zero-width`: Keep zero-width and invisible characters.
- `--keep-odd-spaces`: Keep no-break and other unusual spaces.
- `--keep-spaces`: Do not collapse runs of spaces.
- `--keep-trailing`: Keep spaces at line ends.
- `--trim-leading`: Remove indentation.
- `--trim`: Trim the whole text.
- `--blank-lines <keep|collapse|remove>`: Blank lines. Default: keep.
- `--line-endings <keep|lf|crlf>`: Line endings. Default: keep.
- `--tabs <keep|spaces|tabs>`: Tabs to spaces or back. Default: keep.
- `--tab-size <n>`: Tab width. Default: 4.
- `--quotes <keep|straight|smart|german>`: Quotes. Default: keep.
- `--dashes <keep|ascii|smart>`: Dashes. Default: keep.
- `--ellipsis <keep|ascii|smart>`: Ellipsis. Default: keep.
- `--remove-accents`: é → e.
- `--remove-punctuation`: Remove punctuation.
- `--remove-digits`: Remove digits.
- `--remove-emoji`: Remove emoji.

By default: removes invisible characters, makes unusual spaces plain, collapses runs of spaces and trims line ends.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt whitespace --file pasted.txt --blank-lines collapse --quotes straight
toolbelt whitespace --file pasted.txt --inspect
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/whitespace

### wrap

Hard-wrap text at a width (with an optional prefix such as "> "), or unwrap it.

```
toolbelt wrap [text] [--width <n>] [--prefix <s>] [--no-reflow] [--break-long] [--unwrap]
```

- `-w, --width <n>`: Maximum line width. Default: 80.
- `--prefix <text>`: Added to every line, e.g. "> " or "// ".
- `--no-reflow`: Wrap each line on its own (do not join paragraphs first).
- `--break-long`: Cut words longer than the width.
- `--unwrap`: Join wrapped lines back into paragraphs (removing --prefix).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt wrap --file message.txt --width 72
toolbelt wrap --file quote.txt --width 60 --prefix "> "
toolbelt wrap --file wrapped.txt --unwrap
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/wrap

## Encoding & crypto

### base64

Encode text or a file to Base64, or decode Base64 (standard or URL-safe, data: URIs too).

Aliases: `b64`.

```
toolbelt base64 [text] [--decode] [--url-safe] [--wrap]
```

- `-d, --decode`: Decode instead of encode.
- `--url-safe`: URL-safe alphabet (- _), no padding.
- `--wrap`: Wrap the output at 76 characters (MIME).

Encoding reads --file as raw bytes. Decoded text is printed; decoded binary data is written raw (use --out <path>).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt base64 "hello world"
toolbelt base64 -d aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=
toolbelt base64 --file logo.png   # Encode a file.
toolbelt base64 -d --file logo.b64 --out logo.png   # Decode to a file.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/base64

### base-encodings

Text or bytes to and from hex, binary, octal, decimal, Base32, Base58 and Ascii85.

```
toolbelt base-encodings [text] [--to <enc>] [--from <enc>] [--separator <sep>]
```

- `--to <encoding>`: Encode into this encoding (without --to or --from: every encoding).
- `--from <encoding>`: Decode from this encoding.
- `--separator <space|none|comma|newline>`: Between bytes, for hex / binary / octal / decimal. Default: space.
- `--upper`: Upper-case hex.
- `--padding`: Base32 = padding (--no-padding to drop). Default: true.
- `--delimiters`: Ascii85 <~ ~> delimiters.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt base-encodings "Hi" --to binary
toolbelt base-encodings "48 69" --from hex
toolbelt base-encodings "hello"   # Every encoding at once.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/base-encodings

### url-encode

Percent-encode or decode text as a URL component, a whole URL, or form data.

Aliases: `urlencode`.

```
toolbelt url-encode [text] [--decode] [--mode component|uri|form] [--strict]
```

- `-d, --decode`: Decode instead of encode.
- `-m, --mode <component|uri|form>`: component (encodeURIComponent), uri (encodeURI) or form (spaces as +). Default: component.
- `--strict`: Also escape ! ' ( ) * (RFC 3986).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt url-encode "a b&c=d/é"
toolbelt url-encode -d 'a%20b%26c'
toolbelt url-encode "q=hello world" --mode form
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/url-encode

### url-parser

Split a URL into its parts and decoded query parameters; query string <-> JSON.

Aliases: `url`.

```
toolbelt url-parser <url> [--query-json] [--from-json]
```

- `--query-json`: Print the query string as JSON (repeated keys become arrays, a[b] nests).
- `--from-json`: The input is a JSON object: print it as a query string.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt url-parser 'https://user@example.com:8080/a/b?q=1&q=2#top'
toolbelt url-parser '?a=1&b[c]=x' --query-json
toolbelt url-parser '{"q":"search","page":2}' --from-json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/url-parser

### html-entities

Escape text as HTML entities (unsafe characters, named or numeric), or decode them.

Aliases: `entities`.

```
toolbelt html-entities [text] [--decode] [--mode unsafe|named|numeric] [--hex]
```

- `-d, --decode`: Decode entities instead of encoding.
- `-m, --mode <unsafe|named|numeric>`: unsafe: only & < > " '; named: also &eacute;…; numeric: &#233;… Default: unsafe.
- `--hex`: Numeric references in hex (&#xE9;).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt html-entities '<a href="x">café</a>'
toolbelt html-entities 'café' --mode named
toolbelt html-entities -d '&lt;p&gt; &eacute; &#x1F600;'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/html-entities

### jwt

Decode a JWT: header, payload, time claims and validity; verify an HMAC signature.

```
toolbelt jwt <token> [--secret <secret>] [--secret-encoding text|base64]
```

- `--secret <secret>`: Verify an HS256/384/512 signature with this secret (exit 1 when invalid).
- `--secret-encoding <text|base64>`: How the secret is written. Default: text.

Decoding needs no key: a JWT payload is only Base64URL. The validity is computed against the current time.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt jwt eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjMifQ.sig
toolbelt jwt "$TOKEN" --secret my-secret --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/jwt

### hash

Checksums of a text or file: MD5, SHA-1/256/384/512, SHA3, BLAKE3, CRC32; check one.

```
toolbelt hash [text] [--algo <algo>] [--check <expected>] [--format hex|base64]
```

- `-a, --algo <algo>`: One algorithm (md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3-256, sha3-512, blake3, crc32); every one by default.
- `-c, --check <checksum>`: Compare with an expected checksum (hex, Base64, sha256sum line); exit 1 on mismatch.
- `--format <hex|base64>`: Digest format. Default: hex.
- `--upper`: Upper-case hex.

Text is hashed as UTF-8, exactly as given (stdin keeps its trailing newline). --file hashes the raw bytes.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt hash "abc"
toolbelt hash --file release.zip --algo sha256
toolbelt hash --file release.zip --check 9f86d081884c7d65…   # Which algorithm matches.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/hash

### hmac

HMAC-SHA1/256/384/512 of a message with a key (text, hex or Base64); check a signature.

```
toolbelt hmac [message] --key <key> [--algo sha256] [--format hex|base64|base64url]
```

- `-k, --key <key>`: The secret key (required).
- `-a, --algo <sha1|sha256|sha384|sha512>`: Hash function. Default: sha256.
- `--key-encoding <text|hex|base64>`: How the key is written. Default: text.
- `--message-encoding <text|hex|base64>`: How the message is written. Default: text.
- `--format <hex|base64|base64url>`: Output format. Default: hex.
- `--upper`: Upper-case hex.
- `-c, --check <signature>`: Compare with an expected signature (hex/Base64, sha256= prefix ok); exit 1 on mismatch.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt hmac "hello" --key secret
toolbelt hmac --file body.json --key "$WEBHOOK_SECRET" --check 'sha256=…'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/hmac

### password-hash

Hash a password with bcrypt or Argon2id, verify a password against a hash, or read a hash's parameters.

Aliases: `bcrypt`, `argon2`.

```
toolbelt password-hash <password> [--algo bcrypt|argon2id] [--verify <hash>] [--inspect]
```

- `-a, --algo <bcrypt|argon2id>`: Algorithm. Default: bcrypt.
- `--cost <n>`: bcrypt cost (4–31). Default: 10.
- `--memory <n>`: Argon2 memory in MiB. Default: 19.
- `--iterations <n>`: Argon2 iterations. Default: 2.
- `--parallelism <n>`: Argon2 lanes. Default: 1.
- `--verify <hash>`: Check the password against this bcrypt/Argon2 hash (exit 1 when it does not match).
- `--inspect`: The input is a hash: print its algorithm and parameters.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt password-hash "correct horse" --cost 12
toolbelt password-hash 'correct horse' --verify '$2b$12$…'
toolbelt password-hash '$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$…' --inspect
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/password-hash

### uuid

Generate UUID v4 / v7, ULID or nanoid; or inspect a UUID / ULID (version, time).

Aliases: `ulid`, `nanoid`.

```
toolbelt uuid [id-to-inspect] [--kind v4|v7|ulid|nanoid] [--count <n>]
```

- `-k, --kind <v4|v7|ulid|nanoid>`: What to generate. Default: v4.
- `-n, --count <n>`: How many (1–1000). Default: 1.
- `--upper`: Upper case.
- `--dashes`: UUID dashes (--no-dashes to drop). Default: true.
- `--size <n>`: nanoid length. Default: 21.
- `--alphabet <name|chars>`: nanoid alphabet: url, alnum, lower, hex, digits, nolookalikes, or your own characters. Default: url.

With an argument, inspects it instead: version, variant, embedded timestamp, the ULID/UUID form.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt uuid
toolbelt uuid --kind v7 -n 5
toolbelt uuid --kind nanoid --size 12 --alphabet alnum
toolbelt uuid 0190b3a2-7c4e-7d3a-9f1e-123456789abc   # Inspect an id.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/uuid

### password

Generate secure passwords or passphrases (with their entropy), or rate a password's strength.

Aliases: `passphrase`.

```
toolbelt password [--length <n>] [--passphrase] [--count <n>] [--check <password>]
```

- `-l, --length <n>`: Password length (4–128). Default: 20.
- `-n, --count <n>`: How many. Default: 1.
- `--lower`: Lowercase letters (--no-lower to drop). Default: true.
- `--upper`: Uppercase letters (--no-upper to drop). Default: true.
- `--digits`: Digits (--no-digits to drop). Default: true.
- `--symbols`: Symbols (--no-symbols to drop). Default: true.
- `--exclude-ambiguous`: Leave out I l 1 | O 0 o and quotes.
- `--each-class`: At least one character of each kind (--no-each-class to drop). Default: true.
- `-p, --passphrase`: A passphrase of random words instead.
- `-w, --words <n>`: Passphrase words (3–20). Default: 5.
- `--separator <value>`: Between passphrase words. Default: -.
- `--capitalize`: Capitalize passphrase words.
- `--digit`: Add a digit to one passphrase word.
- `-c, --check <password>`: Estimate this password's strength instead (bits, score 0–4, time to crack).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt password
toolbelt password --length 32 --no-symbols -n 3
toolbelt password --passphrase --words 6 --capitalize
toolbelt password --check 'P@ssw0rd'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/password

### totp

The current TOTP (2FA) code of a Base32 secret or otpauth:// link; or a new secret.

Aliases: `2fa`, `otp`.

```
toolbelt totp <secret|otpauth-uri> [--digits 6] [--period 30] [--algorithm SHA1] [--at <time>]
```

- `--algorithm <SHA1|SHA256|SHA512>`: HMAC algorithm (an otpauth link's own parameters win). Default: SHA1.
- `--digits <n>`: Code length (6–10). Default: 6.
- `--period <n>`: Seconds per code. Default: 30.
- `--at <time>`: Unix seconds or ISO date (default: now).
- `-g, --generate`: Create a new random secret and its otpauth link.
- `--issuer <value>`: Issuer for --generate.
- `--account <value>`: Account name for --generate.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt totp JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP
toolbelt totp 'otpauth://totp/ACME:me@x.com?secret=JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP&issuer=ACME'
toolbelt totp --generate --issuer ACME --account me@example.com
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/totp

### keypair

Generate a key pair (ECDSA, Ed25519, RSA-OAEP, RSA-PSS) as PEM or JWK, with its fingerprint.

```
toolbelt keypair [--algo ecdsa|ed25519|rsa-oaep|rsa-pss] [--curve P-256] [--bits 3072] [--format pem|jwk]
```

- `-a, --algo <ecdsa|ed25519|rsa-oaep|rsa-pss>`: Key type. Default: ecdsa.
- `--curve <P-256|P-384|P-521>`: ECDSA curve. Default: P-256.
- `--bits <2048|3072|4096>`: RSA modulus size. Default: 3072.
- `--format <pem|jwk>`: Output format. Default: pem.

The private key is printed: write it to a file with --out and keep it secret.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt keypair
toolbelt keypair --algo ed25519 --out key.pem
toolbelt keypair --algo rsa-pss --bits 4096 --format jwk
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/keypair

### qr

Make a QR code (text, URL or Wi-Fi) as terminal text or SVG. Reading QR images is browser-only.

Aliases: `qrcode`.

```
toolbelt qr [text] [--format text|svg] [--ecc L|M|Q|H] [--wifi-ssid <name> --wifi-password <pw>]
```

- `--format <text|svg>`: Output. Default: text.
- `--ecc <L|M|Q|H>`: Error correction level. Default: M.
- `--margin <n>`: Quiet zone, in modules. Default: 4.
- `--size <n>`: SVG width and height in pixels. Default: 512.
- `--fg <value>`: SVG dark color. Default: #000000.
- `--bg <value>`: SVG background (empty for transparent). Default: #ffffff.
- `--invert`: Text output for a dark terminal (light modules drawn).
- `--wifi-ssid <value>`: Make a Wi-Fi QR code for this network instead of text.
- `--wifi-password <value>`: Wi-Fi password.
- `--wifi-security <WPA|WEP|nopass>`: Wi-Fi security. Default: WPA.
- `--wifi-hidden`: Hidden network.

Scanning a QR code from an image or the camera needs the browser: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/qr

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt qr https://example.com
toolbelt qr https://example.com --format svg --out qr.svg
toolbelt qr --wifi-ssid Home --wifi-password 's3cret' --format svg --out wifi.svg
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/qr

### data-uri

Turn text or a file into a data: URI (Base64 or percent), or decode a data: URI.

```
toolbelt data-uri [text] [--mime <type>] [--encoding base64|percent] [--decode]
```

- `-d, --decode`: Decode a data: URI (text printed, binary written raw).
- `--mime <type>`: MIME type (default: from the --file name, else text/plain).
- `--encoding <base64|percent>`: Body encoding. Default: base64.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt data-uri "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'/>" --mime image/svg+xml --encoding percent
toolbelt data-uri --file icon.png
toolbelt data-uri -d 'data:text/plain;base64,aGk='
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/data-uri

### encrypt

Encrypt or decrypt text or a file with a password (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 or Argon2id), site-compatible.

```
toolbelt encrypt [text] --password <pw> [--decrypt] [--kdf pbkdf2|argon2id]
```

- `-p, --password <password>`: The password (or set TOOLBELT_PASSWORD, which keeps it out of the shell history).
- `-d, --decrypt`: Decrypt instead of encrypt.
- `--kdf <pbkdf2|argon2id>`: Key derivation. Default: pbkdf2.
- `--iterations <n>`: PBKDF2 iterations. Default: 600000.
- `--wrap`: Wrap the Base64 output at 76 characters.

The output is the site's container as Base64 (starts with VEJFTg): the browser tool decrypts it and vice versa. With --file, the file is encrypted with its name; decrypting a file writes its bytes (use --out).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt encrypt "meet at noon" --password hunter2
TOOLBELT_PASSWORD=hunter2 toolbelt encrypt -d VEJFTgEB…
toolbelt encrypt --file report.pdf -p hunter2 --out report.pdf.enc
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/encrypt

### compress

Compress text or a file with gzip, zlib (deflate) or raw deflate, or decompress (format detected).

Aliases: `gzip`.

```
toolbelt compress [text] [--format gzip|deflate|deflate-raw] [--decompress] [--encoding base64|hex|raw]
```

- `-d, --decompress`: Decompress instead.
- `--format <gzip|deflate|deflate-raw|auto>`: Format (auto: detected, when decompressing). Default: gzip / auto.
- `--encoding <base64|hex|raw>`: Compressed output as Base64, hex or raw bytes (use --out). Default: base64.

Decompressing reads an argument or stdin as Base64/hex text, and --file as raw compressed bytes. Binary results are written raw (use --out).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt compress "hello hello hello"
toolbelt compress --file data.json --encoding raw --out data.json.gz
toolbelt compress -d --file data.json.gz
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/compress

### certificate

Decode X.509 certificates and CSRs (PEM chain or DER): subject, issuer, validity, SAN, key, fingerprints.

Aliases: `cert`, `x509`.

```
toolbelt certificate [pem] [--file cert.pem]
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt certificate --file cert.pem
openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -showcerts </dev/null | toolbelt certificate --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/certificate

### basic-auth

Build an HTTP Basic Authorization header (and curl commands), or decode one back to user and password.

```
toolbelt basic-auth --user <user> --password <pw> [--url <url>] | toolbelt basic-auth <header|token|curl|url>
```

- `-u, --user <value>`: User name (encode).
- `-p, --password <value>`: Password (encode).
- `--url <value>`: URL for the curl examples.

Without --user, decodes the input: an Authorization header, a Base64 token, a curl -u command or a URL with user:password@.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt basic-auth --user alice --password 's3cret'
toolbelt basic-auth 'Authorization: Basic YWxpY2U6czNjcmV0'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/basic-auth

### bip39

Generate a BIP39 mnemonic, validate one (checksum, typos), or convert entropy <-> words and get the seed.

```
toolbelt bip39 [mnemonic] [--words 12] [--entropy <hex>] [--seed] [--passphrase <p>]
```

- `-w, --words <12|15|18|21|24>`: Words to generate. Default: 12.
- `--entropy <hex>`: Turn this entropy (32–64 hex digits) into words.
- `--seed`: Also print the 64-byte seed (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512).
- `--passphrase <value>`: Optional BIP39 passphrase for the seed.

With a mnemonic as input, validates it (exit 1 when invalid). Only the English word list.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt bip39 --words 24
toolbelt bip39 'abandon abandon … about' --seed
toolbelt bip39 --entropy 00000000000000000000000000000000
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/bip39

### safelink

Unwrap Outlook Safe Links / Proofpoint / Google redirects and strip tracking parameters (utm_…).

Aliases: `clean-url`.

```
toolbelt safelink [text-or-url] [--no-unwrap] [--no-strip]
```

- `--unwrap`: Unwrap redirect wrappers (--no-unwrap to keep). Default: true.
- `--strip`: Remove tracking parameters (--no-strip to keep). Default: true.

Every URL in the input is cleaned in place; the rest of the text is kept.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt safelink 'https://example.com/?utm_source=x&id=3'
toolbelt safelink --file email.txt
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/safelink

## Data & formats

### json

Validate, format, minify or sort the keys of JSON (errors with line and column).

```
toolbelt json [text] [--indent 2|4|tab] [--minify] [--sort-keys] [--check]
```

- `--indent <2|4|tab>`: Indentation. Default: 2.
- `-m, --minify`: One line, no spaces.
- `-s, --sort-keys`: Sort object keys (recursively).
- `--check`: Only validate: print a summary instead of the document.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json '{"b":1,"a":[1,2]}' --sort-keys
toolbelt json --file data.json --minify
toolbelt json --file data.json --check   # Exit 1 with line:column if invalid.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/json

### convert

Convert between JSON, YAML and TOML (input format detected, errors located).

Aliases: `yaml`.

```
toolbelt convert [text] [--from auto|json|yaml|toml] [--to json|yaml|toml] [--indent 2|4]
```

- `--from <auto|json|yaml|toml>`: Input format. Default: auto.
- `-t, --to <json|yaml|toml>`: Output format. Default: yaml.
- `--indent <2|4>`: Indentation. Default: 2.

YAML with several documents (---) becomes a JSON array. TOML needs an object at the root and has no null (null keys are dropped).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt convert --file config.yaml --to json
toolbelt convert --file Cargo.toml --to yaml
toolbelt convert '{"name":"app","port":8080}' --to toml
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/convert

### csv

CSV to JSON, or JSON to CSV (direction detected; delimiter, header, typed cells).

```
toolbelt csv [text] [--to json|csv] [--delimiter auto|comma|semicolon|tab|pipe] [--no-header] [--shape objects|arrays] [--no-infer] [--minify]
```

- `-t, --to <json|csv>`: Output format (default: CSV for JSON input, JSON otherwise).
- `-d, --delimiter <auto|comma|semicolon|tab|pipe>`: CSV delimiter (auto: detected when reading, comma when writing). Default: auto.
- `--header`: The first CSV row is a header (read) / write a header row. Use --no-header to turn off. Default: true.
- `--shape <objects|arrays>`: CSV → JSON rows as objects (keyed by header) or arrays. Default: objects.
- `--infer`: Type cells (numbers, booleans, null); --no-infer keeps text. Default: true.
- `-m, --minify`: One-line JSON.

JSON → CSV flattens nested objects into dotted column names (address.city).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt csv --file people.csv   # CSV → JSON array of objects.
toolbelt csv '[{"name":"Ann","address":{"city":"Lyon"}}]'   # JSON → CSV.
toolbelt csv --file export.csv --delimiter semicolon --no-infer
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/csv

### markdown-table

CSV, TSV or a JSON array to an aligned Markdown table, or a Markdown table back to CSV/TSV/JSON.

Aliases: `md-table`.

```
toolbelt markdown-table [text] [--to md|csv|tsv|json] [--align left|center|right|none|<list>] [--compact]
```

- `-t, --to <md|csv|tsv|json>`: Output (default: CSV when the input is a Markdown table, Markdown otherwise).
- `-a, --align <align|list>`: Column alignment for every column, or a comma list per column (left,right,center,none).
- `--compact`: Do not pad the cells.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt markdown-table --file data.csv
toolbelt markdown-table '[{"a":1,"b":2}]' --align right
toolbelt markdown-table --file README.md --to json   # The first table, as JSON.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/markdown-table

### json-to-ts

TypeScript types or a Zod schema inferred from a JSON sample.

```
toolbelt json-to-ts [json] [--to ts|zod] [--root-name <Name>] [--style interface|type] [--readonly]
```

- `-t, --to <ts|zod>`: Output. Default: ts.
- `--root-name <Name>`: Name of the root type. Default: Root.
- `--style <interface|type>`: TypeScript declarations. Default: interface.
- `--readonly`: readonly properties and arrays.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-to-ts '{"id":1,"tags":["a"],"owner":{"name":"Ann"}}'
toolbelt json-to-ts --file response.json --to zod --root-name User
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/json-to-ts

### json-diff

Structural diff of two JSON documents: paths added, removed or changed (key order ignored).

```
toolbelt json-diff <old.json> <new.json> [--a <json>] [--b <json>] [--ignore-array-order] [--only added|removed|changed]
```

- `--a <json>`: The old document, inline (instead of a file).
- `--b <json>`: The new document, inline (instead of a file).
- `--ignore-array-order`: Compare arrays as multisets (order does not matter).
- `--only <added|removed|changed>`: Only this kind of change.
- `--exit-code`: Exit with 1 when the documents differ.

Output: one line per change, `+ $.path: value`, `- $.path: value`, `~ $.path: old → new`.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-diff old.json new.json
toolbelt json-diff --a '{"a":1,"b":[1,2]}' --b '{"a":2,"b":[2,1]}' --ignore-array-order
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/json-diff

### jsonpath

Run a JSONPath query ($.a.b[*], .., [?(@.price < 10)]) on a JSON document.

```
toolbelt jsonpath <query> [json] [--paths]
```

- `-p, --paths`: Print the paths of the matches, not their values.

The document comes after the query, or from --file or stdin. Supports $, .key, ['key'], [n], [-n], [start:end:step], [*], .., unions and filters (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, !, &&, ||).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt jsonpath '$.store.book[*].author' --file store.json
cat data.json | toolbelt jsonpath '$..[?(@.price < 10)].title'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/jsonpath

### sql

Format SQL (many dialects, keyword case) or minify it to one line.

```
toolbelt sql [query] [--dialect <id>] [--keyword-case upper|lower|preserve] [--indent 2|4|tab] [--minify]
```

- `-d, --dialect <dialect>`: sql, postgresql, mysql, mariadb, sqlite, transactsql, plsql, bigquery, snowflake, redshift, duckdb, clickhouse, spark, hive, trino, db2, singlestoredb, tidb, n1ql. Default: sql.
- `--keyword-case <upper|lower|preserve>`: Case of keywords, types and functions. Default: upper.
- `--indent <2|4|tab>`: Indentation. Default: 2.
- `-m, --minify`: One line (strings and comments-hints kept).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt sql "select id, name from users where active = 1 order by name"
toolbelt sql --file query.sql --dialect postgresql --keyword-case lower
toolbelt sql --file query.sql --minify
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/sql

### xml

Validate, format or minify XML (well-formedness errors with line and column).

```
toolbelt xml [text] [--indent 2|4|tab] [--minify] [--remove-comments] [--collapse] [--check]
```

- `--indent <2|4|tab>`: Indentation. Default: 2.
- `-m, --minify`: One line.
- `--remove-comments`: Drop <!-- comments -->.
- `--collapse`: Write empty elements as <tag/>.
- `--check`: Only validate: print element/attribute counts and depth.

XML → JSON is the json-xml command.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt xml '<a><b x="1">hi</b></a>'
toolbelt xml --file feed.xml --check
toolbelt xml --file pom.xml --minify --remove-comments
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/xml

### env

.env to JSON, or a JSON object to .env lines (dotenv rules; duplicates and bad lines reported).

Aliases: `dotenv`.

```
toolbelt env [text] [--to json|env] [--export] [--sort]
```

- `-t, --to <json|env>`: Output (default: .env for JSON input, JSON otherwise).
- `--export`: .env output: prefix lines with `export `.
- `--sort`: Sort the keys.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt env --file .env   # As a JSON object.
toolbelt env '{"PORT":8080,"NAME":"my app"}' --export
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/env

### query-string

A query string (or a whole URL) to JSON, or a JSON object to a query string.

Aliases: `qs`.

```
toolbelt query-string [text] [--to json|query] [--no-plus] [--no-brackets] [--infer]
```

- `-t, --to <json|query>`: Output (default: a query string for JSON input, JSON otherwise).
- `--plus`: Read "+" as a space and write spaces as "+" (forms); --no-plus uses %20. Default: true.
- `--brackets`: Read and write a[b]=1 / a[]=1 as nesting; --no-brackets keeps keys flat. Default: true.
- `--infer`: Turn "1", "true", "null" into numbers, booleans, null.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt query-string 'https://x.io/s?q=hello+world&tag=a&tag=b&page=2' --infer
toolbelt query-string '{"q":"a b","filter":{"tags":["x","y"]}}'
```

### json-to-code

Types inferred from a JSON sample, in Go, Rust, Kotlin, Java, C#, Python, Swift or Dart.

```
toolbelt json-to-code [json] --to go|rust|kotlin|java|csharp|python|swift|dart [--root-name <Name>] [--java record|pojo] [--python dataclass|pydantic]
```

- `-t, --to <go|rust|kotlin|java|csharp|python|swift|dart>`: Target language. Default: go.
- `--root-name <Name>`: Name of the root type. Default: Root.
- `--java <record|pojo>`: Java: records or classes. Default: record.
- `--python <dataclass|pydantic>`: Python: dataclasses or Pydantic v2 models. Default: dataclass.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-to-code '{"id":1,"name":"Ann","tags":["a"]}' --to rust
toolbelt json-to-code --file user.json --to python --python pydantic --root-name User
```

### json-schema

Generate a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) from a sample, or validate a document against a schema.

```
toolbelt json-schema [sample] [--no-formats] [--strict]  |  toolbelt json-schema --validate <schema.json> <doc.json> [--schema <json>] [--doc <json>]
```

- `-V, --validate`: Validate a document (second file or --doc) against a schema (first file or --schema).
- `--schema <json>`: --validate: the schema, inline.
- `--doc <json>`: --validate: the document, inline.
- `--formats`: Generate: add "format" for dates, emails, URIs… Validate: check formats. --no-formats to turn off. Default: true.
- `--strict`: Generate: additionalProperties: false on every object.

--validate exits with 1 when the document does not match, listing each problem with its path.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-schema --file sample.json --strict
toolbelt json-schema --validate schema.json doc.json
toolbelt json-schema --validate --schema '{"type":"integer"}' --doc '"x"'
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/json-schema

HTML or SVG to JSX (className, htmlFor, style objects, camelCase SVG attributes), optionally a component.

Aliases: `jsx`.

```
toolbelt html-to-jsx [html] [--component] [--name <Name>] [--typescript] [--native]
```

- `-c, --component`: Wrap in `export default function Name()`.
- `--name <Name>`: Component name (default: from the markup).
- `--typescript`: Type the component's props.
- `--native`: react-native-svg components (Svg, Path…).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt html-to-jsx '<label for="email" class="label" style="font-size: 12px">Email</label>'
```

### json-tree

Explore a JSON document: an outline with types and sizes, a search in keys and values, every path.

```
toolbelt json-tree [json] [--depth <n>] [--search <text>] [--paths]
```

- `--depth <n>`: Outline depth (deeper containers are summarized). Default: 3.
- `-s, --search <text>`: List the keys and values containing this text (case-insensitive), with their paths.
- `-p, --paths`: List every scalar as `path = value` (greppable).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-tree --file package.json --depth 2
toolbelt json-tree --file data.json --search email
toolbelt json-tree --file data.json --paths | grep price
```

### json-xml

JSON to XML (@attributes, #text, arrays as repeated elements), or XML to JSON (direction detected).

```
toolbelt json-xml [text] [--to xml|json] [--root <name>] [--indent 2|4|tab|min] [--declaration] [--no-typed]
```

- `-t, --to <xml|json>`: Output (default: XML for JSON input, JSON for XML input).
- `--root <name>`: JSON → XML: root element (default: the single top-level key, else root).
- `--indent <2|4|tab|min>`: Indentation (min: one line). Default: 2.
- `--declaration`: JSON → XML: start with <?xml version="1.0"…?>.
- `--typed`: XML → JSON: numbers, booleans and null as JSON values; --no-typed keeps text. Default: true.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt json-xml '{"note":{"@id":"7","to":"Ann","body":"Hi"}}'
toolbelt json-xml --file feed.xml   # XML → JSON.
```

docker run commands to a docker-compose.yml (ports, volumes, env, networks…).

## Time & numbers

### timestamp

Unix timestamp ↔ date: ISO 8601, RFC 2822, every unit, day of year, ISO week, relative.

Aliases: `epoch`.

```
toolbelt timestamp [timestamp|date] [--unit auto|s|ms|us|ns] [--zone <zone>]
```

- `-u, --unit <auto|s|ms|us|ns>`: Unit of a numeric timestamp. Default: auto.
- `-z, --zone <zone>`: Time zone (IANA name, or a city/abbreviation like paris, est). Default: UTC.

Without input: the current time. Dates without an offset are read in --zone.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt timestamp 1700000000
toolbelt timestamp "2024-01-31 12:00" --zone Europe/Paris
toolbelt timestamp --json   # Now, every format.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/timestamp

### timezones

Convert a date and time from one time zone to others (DST-aware).

Aliases: `tz`.

```
toolbelt timezones [YYYY-MM-DD] [HH:mm] [--from <zone>] [--to <zone> ...] [--search <query>]
```

- `--from <zone>`: Source zone (IANA name or city). Default: UTC.
- `-t, --to <zone>`: Target zone(s), repeatable or comma-separated.
- `--search <query>`: List zones matching a city, abbreviation or offset.

Without a date or time: now in the source zone.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt timezones 2026-03-10 09:00 --from Europe/Paris --to America/New_York --to Asia/Tokyo
toolbelt timezones 14:30 --from est --to paris,tokyo
toolbelt timezones --search new york
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/timezones

### date-calc

Days, weeks, months and business days between dates; add or subtract a duration or working days.

Aliases: `dates`.

```
toolbelt date-calc <start> [end] [--include-end] | toolbelt date-calc [start] [--years n] [--months n] [--weeks n] [--days n] [--hours n] [--minutes n] [--workdays n] [--subtract]
```

- `--include-end`: Count the end date as a whole day.
- `--years <n>`: Add this many years.
- `--months <n>`: Add this many months.
- `--weeks <n>`: Add this many weeks.
- `--days <n>`: Add this many days.
- `--hours <n>`: Add this many hours.
- `--minutes <n>`: Add this many minutes.
- `--workdays <n>`: Add this many working days (Mon–Fri).
- `--subtract`: Subtract the duration instead of adding it.

Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, optionally with a time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm). With one date and no duration: from today (UTC) to that date.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt date-calc 2026-01-01 2026-12-31
toolbelt date-calc 2026-03-01 --days 90
toolbelt date-calc 2026-03-02 --workdays 10 --subtract
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/date-calc

### cron

Explain a cron expression in plain language and list its next runs.

```
toolbelt cron "<expression>" [--next <n>] [--zone <zone>] [--from <date>]
```

- `-n, --next <n>`: How many next runs to list (0 to 100). Default: 5.
- `-z, --zone <zone>`: Time zone (IANA name, or a city/abbreviation like paris, est). Default: UTC.
- `--from <date>`: Start from this date instead of now.

5 fields (minute hour day month weekday), 6 with seconds first, or a macro (@daily, @hourly…). The description follows --lang.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt cron "0 9 * * 1-5"
toolbelt cron "*/15 * * * *" --next 3 --zone Europe/Paris --json
toolbelt cron "@weekly" --lang fr
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/cron

### number-base

Convert integers between bases 2–36 (any size), with two's complement.

```
toolbelt number-base <number> [--from <base>] [--to <base>] [--bits 8|16|32|64|128] [--group] [--lower]
```

- `--from <n>`: Base of the input (default 10, or from a 0x/0b/0o prefix).
- `--to <n>`: Only print the number in this base.
- `--bits <n>`: Show the two's complement pattern in this width.
- `--group`: Group digits (4 for binary/hex, 3 otherwise).
- `--lower`: Lowercase letters.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt number-base 255
toolbelt number-base 0xff --to 2
toolbelt number-base -1 --bits 16
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/number-base

### bytes

Convert data sizes (bits, SI kB/MB/GB, IEC KiB/MiB/GiB) and compute transfer times.

```
toolbelt bytes <value>[unit] [--unit <unit>] [--to <unit>] [--rate <n unit/s>]
```

- `--unit <unit>`: Unit of the value (bit, kbit, Mbit, B, kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB). Default: B.
- `--to <unit>`: Only print the value in this unit.
- `--rate <n unit>`: Transfer rate, e.g. "100 Mbit/s" (kbit/s, Mbit/s, Gbit/s, kB/s, MB/s, GB/s, KiB/s, MiB/s).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt bytes 1.5GB
toolbelt bytes 1 GiB --to MB
toolbelt bytes 4.7 GB --rate "100 Mbit/s"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/bytes

### roman

Numbers ↔ Roman numerals (1 to 3999), with a strict check.

```
toolbelt roman <number|numeral>
```

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt roman 1990
toolbelt roman MMXXVI
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/roman

### number-words

Write a number out in words (English, French, German): cardinal, ordinal, or an amount of money.

```
toolbelt number-words <number> [--language en|fr|de] [--currency eur|usd] [--ordinal] [--variant fr|be|ch] [--reform]
```

- `--language <en|fr|de>`: Language of the words (default: --lang).
- `-c, --currency <eur|usd>`: Write an amount of money.
- `--ordinal`: Ordinal (first, premier, erste).
- `--variant <fr|be|ch>`: French tens: France, Belgium (septante, nonante), Switzerland (huitante). Default: fr.
- `--reform`: French 1990 spelling (hyphens everywhere).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt number-words 1234.56
toolbelt number-words 1234.56 --language fr --currency eur
toolbelt number-words 21 --ordinal --language de
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/number-words

### percentage

Everyday percentages: X % of Y, X is what % of Y, change, add, reverse, difference.

Aliases: `percent`.

```
toolbelt percentage <of|what|change|add|reverse|diff> <x> <y>
```

of X Y: X % of Y. what X Y: X is what % of Y. change X Y: % change from X to Y. add X Y: Y plus X % (negative X subtracts). reverse X Y: the value before a change of X % that gave Y. diff X Y: % difference (relative to the mean).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt percentage of 15 200
toolbelt percentage change 80 100
toolbelt percentage reverse 20 120   # 120 after +20 % was 100.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/percentage

### units

Convert units: length, mass, temperature, volume, area, speed, time, energy, pressure, data rate.

```
toolbelt units <value> <from> [to] [--category <id>] | toolbelt units --list [--category <id>]
```

- `--category <id>`: Category, when a unit id is ambiguous.
- `-l, --list`: List the categories and their units.

Without a target unit: the value in every unit of its category.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt units 5 km mi
toolbelt units 100 f c   # Fahrenheit to Celsius.
toolbelt units 1 m   # 1 metre in every length unit.
toolbelt units --list --category temperature
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/units

### aspect-ratio

Simplify a width × height to its aspect ratio, find the nearest common one, resize keeping it.

Aliases: `ratio`.

```
toolbelt aspect-ratio <width>x<height> [--width <n> | --height <n>]
```

- `--width <n>`: Resize to this width (prints the height).
- `--height <n>`: Resize to this height (prints the width).

Examples:

```sh

toolbelt aspect-ratio 16:9 --width 1280
```

## Web & dev

### color

Convert a CSS color to every format (hex, rgb, hsl, hwb, lab, lch, oklab, oklch) and check contrast (WCAG, APCA).

```
toolbelt color <color> [--bg <color> | --fg <color>] [--scale]
```

- `--bg <color>`: Check the contrast of the color (as text) on this background.
- `--fg <color>`: Check the contrast of this text color on the color (as background).
- `--scale`: Also list 5 shades and 5 tints.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt color "#0f766e"
toolbelt color '#777' --bg white   # WCAG ratio and APCA Lc of gray text on white.

```


- `-t, --to <unit>`: Only this unit.
- `-u, --unit <unit>`: Unit of a bare number. Default: px.
- `--root <n>`: Root font size in px (1rem). Default: 16.
- `--parent <n>`: Parent font size in px (1em, 100%). Default: 16.
- `--vw <n>`: Viewport width in px. Default: 1440.
- `--vh <n>`: Viewport height in px. Default: 900.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt css-units 24px
```

### semver

Semantic versions (npm rules): parse, compare, check a range, max satisfying, bump.


- `-c, --compare <version>`: Compare the version with this one.

### commit

Build a Conventional Commits message (and its git commit command), with checks.

```
toolbelt commit "<description>" [--type <type>] [--scope <scope>] [--body <text>] [--breaking [--breaking-note <text>]] [--closes <refs>] [--footer <line>...] [--command]
```

- `-t, --type <type>`: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert… Default: feat.
- `-s, --scope <scope>`: What the change touches.
- `-b, --body <text>`: Longer explanation.
- `--breaking`: A breaking change (adds ! to the header).
- `--breaking-note <text>`: What breaks and how to migrate (BREAKING CHANGE footer).
- `--closes <refs>`: Issues closed: "12, #34, org/repo#5".
- `--footer <line>`: A footer ("Refs: #7"); repeatable.
- `--no-wrap`: Keep the body as typed (no wrap at 72).
- `--command`: Print the git commit command instead.

Errors (missing description, bad type…) exit with 1; warnings go to stderr.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt commit "add dark mode" --type feat --scope ui
toolbelt commit "drop node 18" --type build --breaking --breaking-note "Node 20 is required" --closes 42 --command
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/commit

```sh
toolbelt ip-tools 3232235777   # 192.168.1.1 in every notation.
toolbelt ip-tools "10.0.0.5 - 10.0.0.20"   # The smallest CIDR list for a range.
toolbelt ip-tools 10.1.2.3 --in 10.0.0.0/8 --in 192.168.0.0/16
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/ip-tools

### mac-address

Generate random MAC addresses, or inspect ones (format, unicast/multicast, local, EUI-64).

Aliases: `mac`.

```
toolbelt mac-address [mac...] | [--count <n>] [--prefix <oui>] [--universal] [--multicast] [--format <f>] [--upper]
```

- `-n, --count <n>`: How many to generate. Default: 1.
- `--prefix <bytes>`: Fixed first bytes (an OUI), e.g. 00:1A:2B.
- `--universal`: Clear the locally-administered bit (default: local).
- `--multicast`: Set the multicast bit (default: unicast).
- `--format <colon|dash|dot|none>`: Notation. Default: colon.
- `--upper`: Uppercase hex.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt mac-address --count 3
toolbelt mac-address 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E
toolbelt mac-address --prefix 00:1A:2B --format dash --upper
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/mac-address

### ipv6-ula

IPv6 Unique Local Address prefix (RFC 4193): generate a random /48, or inspect one, with /64 subnets.

Aliases: `ula`.

```
toolbelt ipv6-ula [global-id|address] [--subnets <n>] [--start <n>]
```

- `--subnets <n>`: How many /64 subnets to list. Default: 4.
- `--start <n>`: First subnet id (0-65535). Default: 0.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt ipv6-ula   # A new random prefix.
toolbelt ipv6-ula fd12:3456:789a::/48 --subnets 8
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/ipv6-ula

### random-port

Pick random free-looking ports (skipping well-known and common ones), or look up common ports.

Aliases: `port`.

```
toolbelt random-port [--count <n>] [--range registered|dynamic|unprivileged] [--min <p> --max <p>] | <port|words>
```

- `-n, --count <n>`: How many ports. Default: 1.
- `--range <registered|dynamic|unprivileged>`: IANA range to pick from (1024-49151, 49152-65535, 1024-65535). Default: registered.
- `--min <n>`: Custom range start.
- `--max <n>`: Custom range end.
- `--allow-common`: Do not skip the commonly used ports.
- `--allow-well-known`: Do not skip ports below 1024.
- `--avoid-ephemeral`: Skip Linux's ephemeral range 32768-60999.
- `--proto <all|tcp|udp>`: Lookup: protocol. Default: all.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt random-port --count 3
toolbelt random-port 5432   # What usually listens on 5432.
toolbelt random-port postgres
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/random-port

### git-cheatsheet

Find the git command for a task, in plain words ("undo last commit", "rename a branch").

Aliases: `git`.

```
toolbelt git-cheatsheet <what you want to do> [--group <g>] [--danger] [--limit <n>]
```

- `--group <setup|commit|inspect|branches|undo|stash|rebase|remote|tags|worktrees|bisect|cleanup>`: Only this theme.
- `--danger`: Only commands that can lose work or rewrite history.
- `--limit <n>`: Max tips shown (default 5 for a search, all otherwise).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt git-cheatsheet "undo the last commit"
toolbelt git-cheatsheet --group stash
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/git-cheatsheet

### email-normalize

Validate and normalize email addresses (case, Gmail dots, +tags, IDN), and dedupe a list.

Aliases: `email`.

```
toolbelt email-normalize <addresses> [--keep-case] [--no-providers] [--plus-all] [--punycode] [--unique]
```

- `--keep-case`: Do not lowercase the local part.
- `--providers`: Provider rules (Gmail dots, +tags at known providers). Default: true.
- `--plus-all`: Drop +tags at every domain.
- `--punycode`: Write domains in punycode (xn--…).
- `-u, --unique`: Print only the unique valid normalized addresses.

Addresses are separated by new lines, commas or semicolons; Name <addr> and mailto: are accepted. Exits with 1 if any address is invalid.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt email-normalize "John.Doe+news@GoogleMail.com, jane@exämple.de"
toolbelt email-normalize --file contacts.txt --unique
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/email-normalize

### http-headers

HTTP headers reference search, or a security check of raw response headers (curl -I output).

Aliases: `headers`.

```
toolbelt http-headers <words> [--kind request|response] [--category <c>] | --check [headers]
```

- `--check`: Check response headers (argument, --file or stdin) against security recommendations.
- `--kind <all|request|response>`: Reference: only these. Default: all.
- `--category <security|cors|caching|conditional|content|auth|cookies|connection|context|misc>`: Reference: only this category.

With --check, exits with 1 when a problem (level bad) is found.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt http-headers cache
curl -sI https://example.com | toolbelt http-headers --check
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/http-headers

### curl-convert

Convert a curl command to fetch, axios, Python requests, Go, PHP, wget or HTTPie code.

Aliases: `curl`.

```
toolbelt curl-convert '<curl command>' [--to <target>]
```

- `-t, --to <fetch|axios|python|go|php|wget|httpie>`: Target language. Default: fetch.

Quote the curl command as one argument, or pass it after -- (each word is re-quoted), with --file, or on stdin. Warnings go to stderr.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt curl-convert 'curl -X POST https://api.example.com/items -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"a\":1}"' --to python
toolbelt curl-convert --to go -- curl -L https://example.com
```

## CSS & design

### box-shadow

Generate a CSS box-shadow (one layer from flags, a preset, or layers as JSON).

```
toolbelt box-shadow [--x <px>] [--y <px>] [--blur <px>] [--spread <px>] [--color <c>] [--alpha <0-1>] [--inset] [--preset <id>] [--layers <json>] [--format css|tailwind|value]
```

- `--x <n>`: Horizontal offset (px). Default: 0.
- `--y <n>`: Vertical offset (px). Default: 4.
- `--blur <n>`: Blur radius (px). Default: 12.
- `--spread <n>`: Spread (px). Default: 0.
- `--color <color>`: Shadow color. Default: #000000.
- `--alpha <n>`: Opacity, 0 to 1. Default: 0.15.
- `--inset`: Inner shadow.
- `--preset <id>`: soft, elevated, floating, sharp, neumorphism, pressed, glow, ring, layered.
- `--layers <json>`: Several layers: [{"x":0,"y":4,"blur":12,"spread":0,"color":"#000","alpha":0.2,"inset":false}, …].
- `--format <css|tailwind|value>`: Output: a CSS declaration, Tailwind classes, or the bare value. Default: css.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt box-shadow --y 8 --blur 24 --alpha 0.2
toolbelt box-shadow --preset neumorphism --format tailwind
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/box-shadow

### gradient

Generate a CSS gradient (linear, radial, conic) from colors or a preset.

```
toolbelt gradient <color[ pos%]>... [--type linear|radial|conic] [--angle <deg>] [--space oklch|oklab|srgb|hsl|none] [--preset <id>] [--format css|tailwind|value]
```

- `--type <linear|radial|conic>`: Gradient type. Default: linear.
- `--angle <n>`: Angle in degrees (linear; start angle for conic). Default: 135.
- `--shape <ellipse|circle>`: Radial shape. Default: ellipse.
- `--x <n>`: Center x in % (radial, conic). Default: 50.
- `--y <n>`: Center y in % (radial, conic). Default: 50.
- `--repeating`: repeating-*-gradient.
- `--space <oklch|oklab|srgb|hsl|none>`: Interpolation color space (none = browser default, no `in …`). Default: oklch.
- `--hue <shorter|longer>`: Hue path for oklch/hsl. Default: shorter.
- `--preset <id>`: sunset, ocean, mint, aurora, spotlight, rainbow, stripes, pie.
- `--format <css|tailwind|value>`: Output: a CSS declaration, Tailwind classes, or the bare value. Default: css.

Stops are colors, optionally followed by a position in %: "#f97316 0" "#db2777 55". Without positions they are spread evenly.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt gradient "#0f766e" "#f59e0b" --angle 90
toolbelt gradient "red 0" "gold 40" "blue 100" --type radial --space none
toolbelt gradient --preset sunset --format tailwind
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/gradient

### border-radius

Normalize a border-radius (up to 8 values), use a blob preset, or draw a random blob.

Aliases: `blob`.

```
toolbelt border-radius [value] [--preset <id>] [--random] [--seed <n>] [--format css|tailwind|value]
```

- `--preset <id>`: blob, pebble, circle, egg, leaf, drop, tab, rounded.
- `--random`: A random organic blob.
- `--seed <n>`: Seed for --random (reproducible).
- `--format <css|tailwind|value>`: Output: a CSS declaration, Tailwind classes, or the bare value. Default: css.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt border-radius "30% 70% 70% 30% / 30% 30% 70% 70%"
toolbelt border-radius --preset egg --format tailwind
toolbelt border-radius --random --seed 7
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/border-radius

### cubic-bezier

Parse or pick a cubic-bezier() easing and print its CSS, with sampled progress values.

Aliases: `easing`.

```
toolbelt cubic-bezier [value] [--preset <id>] [--duration <ms>] [--format css|tailwind|value]
```

- `--preset <id>`: ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, in-sine … in-out-back (easings.net names).
- `--duration <n>`: Transition duration in ms (CSS output). Default: 1000.
- `--format <css|tailwind|value>`: Output: a CSS declaration, Tailwind classes, or the bare value. Default: css.

The value can be a keyword (ease-in-out), cubic-bezier(a, b, c, d), or four numbers.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt cubic-bezier 0.34 1.56 0.64 1
toolbelt cubic-bezier "ease-in-out" --format tailwind
toolbelt cubic-bezier --preset out-back --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/cubic-bezier

### clip-path

Generate a CSS clip-path: polygon (points, regular polygon, star, preset), circle, ellipse or inset.

```
toolbelt clip-path [--shape polygon|circle|ellipse|inset] [--points <list>] [--sides <n>] [--star <n>] [--preset <id>] [--format css|tailwind|value]
```

- `--shape <polygon|circle|ellipse|inset>`: Shape kind. Default: polygon.
- `--points <x y, x y, …>`: Polygon points in %: "50 0, 100 100, 0 100".
- `--sides <n>`: A regular polygon with n sides (3–64).
- `--star <n>`: A star with n branches (3–32).
- `--preset <id>`: triangle, trapezoid, parallelogram, rhombus, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, star, cross, arrow-right, chevron, message, frame.
- `--r <n>`: Circle radius (%). Default: 50.
- `--rx <n>`: Ellipse x radius (%). Default: 50.
- `--ry <n>`: Ellipse y radius (%). Default: 35.
- `--cx <n>`: Center x (%). Default: 50.
- `--cy <n>`: Center y (%). Default: 50.
- `--inset <t r b l>`: Inset in % (1 to 4 values). Default: 10 10 10 10.
- `--round <n>`: Inset corner radius (px). Default: 16.
- `--format <css|tailwind|value>`: Output: a CSS declaration, Tailwind classes, or the bare value. Default: css.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt clip-path --preset hexagon
toolbelt clip-path --sides 6
toolbelt clip-path --shape circle --r 40 --format tailwind
toolbelt clip-path --points "50 0, 100 100, 0 100"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/clip-path

### glassmorphism

Generate a frosted-glass card (background, backdrop-filter, border, shadow).

Aliases: `glass`.

```
toolbelt glassmorphism [--preset <id>] [--blur <px>] [--alpha <0-1>] [--saturation <%>] [--tint <color>] [--border <0-1>] [--radius <px>] [--shadow <0-1>] [--format css|tailwind]
```

- `--preset <id>`: frosted, clear, milky, dark, tinted.
- `--blur <n>`: Backdrop blur (px, 0–64). Default: 16.
- `--alpha <n>`: Fill opacity (0–1). Default: 0.18.
- `--saturation <n>`: Backdrop saturate (%, 0–400). Default: 180.
- `--tint <color>`: Fill color. Default: #ffffff.
- `--border <n>`: Border opacity (0–1, 0 = none). Default: 0.3.
- `--radius <n>`: Corner radius (px, 0–100). Default: 20.
- `--shadow <n>`: Shadow opacity (0–1, 0 = none). Default: 0.2.

Generate a CSS triangle, with transparent borders or clip-path.

Aliases: `triangle`.


- `-d, --direction <dir>`: Where the triangle points: up, down, left, right, up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right. Default: up.
- `--width <n>`: Width (px, 1–1000). Default: 80.
- `--height <n>`: Height (px, 1–1000). Default: 60.
- `--equilateral`: Set the height (or width for left/right) for an equilateral triangle.
- `--color <color>`: Fill color. Default: #0f766e.

### svg-placeholder

Generate a placeholder image as SVG markup or a data URI.

Aliases: `placeholder`.

```
toolbelt svg-placeholder [WxH] [--text <t>] [--bg <color>] [--fg <color>] [--font sans|serif|mono] [--size <px>] [--no-bold] [--format svg|data-uri|base64]
```

- `--text <value>`: Label (default: "W×H").
- `--bg <color>`: Background color. Default: #e2e8f0.
- `--fg <color>`: Text color. Default: #64748b.
- `--font <sans|serif|mono>`: Font family. Default: sans.
- `--size <n>`: Font size in px (0 = fit). Default: 0.
- `--bold`: Semi-bold text (--no-bold to turn off). Default: true.
- `--format <svg|data-uri|base64>`: SVG markup, a compact data URI, or a Base64 data URI. Default: svg.

```sh

```

### type-scale

Generate a modular type scale (fluid clamp() or static rem) as CSS variables or Tailwind.

```
toolbelt type-scale [--base <px>] [--ratio <r>] [--min-base <px>] [--min-ratio <r>] [--up <n>] [--down <n>] [--static] [--format css|tailwind4|tailwind3|table]
```

- `--base <n>`: Base size at the large viewport (px). Default: 18.
- `--ratio <n>`: Ratio at the large viewport (1.2 minor third, 1.25 major third, 1.333, 1.5, 1.618…). Default: 1.25.
- `--min-base <n>`: Base size at the small viewport (px, fluid). Default: 16.
- `--min-ratio <n>`: Ratio at the small viewport (fluid). Default: 1.2.
- `--up <n>`: Steps above the base (0–12). Default: 5.
- `--down <n>`: Steps below the base (0–6). Default: 2.
- `--root <n>`: Root font size (px) for rem. Default: 16.
- `--min-vw <n>`: Small viewport width (px). Default: 360.
- `--max-vw <n>`: Large viewport width (px). Default: 1280.
- `--prefix <value>`: Variable prefix (--<prefix>-<n>). Default: step.
- `--static`: One size per step (no clamp()).
- `--format <css|tailwind4|tailwind3|table>`: CSS variables, Tailwind v4 @theme, Tailwind v3 config, or a table of sizes. Default: css.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt type-scale --base 16 --ratio 1.333 --static
toolbelt type-scale --format tailwind4
toolbelt type-scale --format table
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/type-scale

### palette

A 50–950 color scale and harmonies from one color, as CSS variables, Tailwind or JSON, with WCAG hints.

```
toolbelt palette <color> [--harmony <kind>] [--name <n>] [--color-format hex|oklch] [--no-keep-base] [--format css|tailwind4|tailwind3|json|table]
```

- `--harmony <complementary|analogous|triadic|split|tetradic|monochrome>`: Harmony to compute. Default: complementary.
- `--name <value>`: Color name for variables. Default: primary.
- `--color-format <hex|oklch>`: How colors are written. Default: hex.
- `--keep-base`: The nearest step is the base color itself (--no-keep-base to compute it). Default: true.
- `--format <css|tailwind4|tailwind3|json|table>`: CSS variables, Tailwind v4/v3, JSON, or a table with contrast (WCAG) hints. Default: css.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt palette "#3b82f6"
toolbelt palette "#0f766e" --name brand --format tailwind4
toolbelt palette tomato --harmony triadic --format table
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/palette
