## Everyday calculators

### calculator

Evaluate expressions (no eval): functions, %, variables, ans, sum; one expression per line.

Aliases: `calc`.

```
toolbelt calculator "<expression>" [--angle deg|rad] [--decimal-comma]
```

- `--angle <deg|rad>`: Angle unit for trigonometry. Default: deg.
- `--decimal-comma`: Read "1,5" as one and a half (use ";" between arguments).

A file or stdin is a sheet: one expression per line, `x = 3` defines a variable, `ans` is the last result, `sum`/`total` add the lines above, `# comments`. Exit code 1 when a line fails.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt calculator "2 * (3 + 4)^2 / sqrt(16)"
toolbelt calculator "200 + 10%"
toolbelt calculator --file budget.txt
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/calculator

### vat

VAT: from the net price, the gross price or the tax; the rate from two prices; invoice totals.

```
toolbelt vat <amount> [--from net|gross|vat] [--rate <r> | --country <id>] | toolbelt vat --net <n> --gross <g> | toolbelt vat --invoice [--file lines.txt] | toolbelt vat --rates
```

- `--from <net|gross|vat>`: What the amount is. Default: net.
- `-r, --rate <n>`: VAT rate, %.
- `-c, --country <id>`: Use this country's standard rate (fr, be, ch, lu, de, es, it, pt, nl, at, ie, uk, ca, ma). Default: fr.
- `--net <n>`: With --gross: find the rate.
- `--gross <n>`: With --net: find the rate.
- `--invoice`: Invoice lines from the input: "quantity price [rate]" per line (prices before tax, or with tax with --from gross).
- `--rates`: List the countries and their rates.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt vat 100 --rate 20
toolbelt vat 120 --from gross --country fr
toolbelt vat --net 100 --gross 119
printf "2 49.90 20\n1 12 5.5\n" | toolbelt vat --invoice
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/vat

### salary

French gross ↔ net salary estimate (status presets, part time, 13th month, withholding tax), or pay per hour/day/week/month/year.

```
toolbelt salary <amount> [--from gross|net] [--period hour|month|year] [--status non-cadre|cadre|public|portage] [--tax <r>] | toolbelt salary <amount> --pay-period hour|day|week|month|year
```

- `--from <gross|net>`: Whether the amount is gross or net. Default: gross.
- `--period <hour|month|year>`: Period of the amount. Default: month.
- `--status <non-cadre|cadre|public|portage>`: Contribution preset. Default: non-cadre.
- `--employee-rate <n>`: Employee contributions, % of gross (overrides the preset).
- `--fee <n>`: Portage management fee, %. Default: 8.
- `--part-time <n>`: Part-time share, %. Default: 100.
- `--months <n>`: Salaries per year (13 with a 13th month). Default: 12.
- `--tax <n>`: Withholding tax rate, %. Default: 0.
- `--pay-period <hour|day|week|month|year>`: Any country: convert pay from this period.
- `--hours-per-week <n>`: With --pay-period. Default: 40.
- `--days-per-week <n>`: With --pay-period. Default: 5.
- `--weeks-per-year <n>`: With --pay-period (paid weeks). Default: 52.

The French estimate uses flat average contribution rates: it is not a payslip.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt salary 3000 --status cadre
toolbelt salary 2000 --from net --months 13 --tax 5
toolbelt salary 25 --pay-period hour --hours-per-week 35
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/salary

### loan

Loan or mortgage: monthly payment, insurance, total cost, yearly amortization; or how much you can borrow.

Aliases: `mortgage`.

```
toolbelt loan <amount> --rate <r> [--years n | --months n] [--insurance r] [--fees n] [--schedule] | toolbelt loan --budget <monthly> --rate <r> [--years n]
```

- `-r, --rate <n>`: Nominal annual rate, %.
- `-y, --years <n>`: Duration in years. Default: 20.
- `--months <n>`: Duration in months (instead of --years).
- `--insurance <n>`: Annual insurance rate on the initial capital, %. Default: 0.
- `--fees <n>`: One-off fees. Default: 0.
- `--schedule`: Print the amortization by year.
- `--budget <n>`: Monthly budget (insurance included): print the borrowing capacity.
- `--income <n>`: Net monthly income: capacity at a 35 % debt ratio (without --budget).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt loan 200000 --rate 3.5 --years 20 --insurance 0.3
toolbelt loan 15000 --rate 5 --months 48 --schedule
toolbelt loan --budget 1200 --rate 3.5 --years 25
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/loan

### savings

Compound interest with monthly contributions, inflation and a yearly table.

Aliases: `compound`.

```
toolbelt savings [initial] [--monthly n] [--rate r] [--years n] [--compounding yearly|quarterly|monthly|daily] [--start-of-month] [--inflation r]
```

- `--initial <n>`: Starting amount. Default: 0.
- `-m, --monthly <n>`: Monthly contribution. Default: 0.
- `-r, --rate <n>`: Nominal annual rate, %. Default: 3.
- `-y, --years <n>`: Duration in years. Default: 10.
- `--compounding <yearly|quarterly|monthly|daily>`: Compounding frequency. Default: yearly.
- `--start-of-month`: Contributions at the start of each month.
- `--inflation <n>`: Yearly inflation, % (result in today's money). Default: 0.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt savings 1000 --monthly 100 --rate 3 --years 10
toolbelt savings --monthly 200 --rate 5 --years 30 --compounding monthly --inflation 2 --json
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/savings

### tip

Tip and bill splitting: even split with rounding, or uneven by what each person ordered.

```
toolbelt tip <bill> [--tip %] [--people n] [--round step] | toolbelt tip <bill> --own name=amount ...
```

- `-t, --tip <n>`: Tip, % of the bill. Default: 10.
- `-p, --people <n>`: Number of people. Default: 1.
- `--round <n>`: Round each share up to a multiple of this (0 = no rounding). Default: 0.
- `--own <name=amount>`: What one person ordered (repeatable): uneven split; the rest is shared.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt tip 84 --tip 10 --people 4
toolbelt tip 84 --people 4 --round 5
toolbelt tip 100 --tip 15 --own Ann=30 --own Bob=25 --own Cy=20
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/tip

### discount

Discounts: final price after stacked discounts, discount %, original price; compare unit prices.

```
toolbelt discount <price> --off <%> [--off <%> ...] | toolbelt discount <price> --sale <price> | toolbelt discount --sale <price> --off <%> | toolbelt discount --compare "<price> <qty><unit>" ...
```

- `--off <percent>`: A discount, % (repeatable, applied one after the other).
- `--sale <n>`: The sale price.
- `--compare "<price> [packs x]<qty> <unit>"`: A product to compare by unit price (repeatable), e.g. "2.49 500g", "4.20 6x33cl".

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt discount 80 --off 30 --off 10
toolbelt discount 80 --sale 60
toolbelt discount --compare "2.49 500g" --compare "4.20 1kg"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/discount

### bmi

Body mass index, category, healthy weight range; basal metabolic rate and daily calories.

```
toolbelt bmi <kg> <cm> [--age n --sex male|female --activity <level>] | toolbelt bmi <lb> --imperial --feet n --inches n
```

- `--weight <n>`: Weight (kg, or lb with --imperial).
- `--height <n>`: Height (cm, or inches with --imperial).
- `--imperial`: Pounds and feet/inches.
- `--feet <n>`: Height, feet (with --imperial).
- `--inches <n>`: Height, extra inches (with --imperial).
- `--age <n>`: Age, for BMR and calories.
- `--sex <male|female>`: For BMR. Default: female.
- `--activity <sedentary|light|moderate|active|very>`: Activity level. Default: light.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt bmi 70 175
toolbelt bmi 70 175 --age 30 --sex male --activity moderate
toolbelt bmi 154 --imperial --feet 5 --inches 9
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/bmi

### age

Exact age from a birth date, totals in months/weeks/days, next birthday, day milestones; the date at a given age.

```
toolbelt age <YYYY-MM-DD> [--on <YYYY-MM-DD>] | toolbelt age <YYYY-MM-DD> --at <n> [--unit days|weeks|months|years]
```

- `--on <date>`: Reference date (default: today, UTC).
- `--at <n>`: Print the date at this age.
- `--unit <days|weeks|months|years>`: Unit of --at. Default: days.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt age 1990-05-15
toolbelt age 1990-05-15 --at 10000 --unit days
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/age

### fuel

Trip fuel or charging cost (L/100 km, mpg, kWh), per person; or consumption from liters and km.

```
toolbelt fuel <distance> [--consumption n] [--unit l100|mpgUS|mpgUK|kmL] [--price n] [--people n] [--round-trip] [--ev] | toolbelt fuel --liters n --km n
```

- `--distance <n>`: Trip distance.
- `--distance-unit <km|mi>`: Unit of the distance. Default: km.
- `--consumption <n>`: Consumption (default 6.5 L/100 km, or 17 kWh/100 km with --ev).
- `--unit <l100|mpgUS|mpgUK|kmL|kwh100|whkm|miKwh|kwh100mi>`: Unit of the consumption.
- `--price <n>`: Price per liter (or per kWh with --ev). Default: 1.85.
- `--price-unit <L|galUS|galUK>`: Unit of the fuel price. Default: L.
- `--people <n>`: Split the cost between this many people. Default: 1.
- `--round-trip`: Double the distance.
- `--ev`: Electric vehicle (kWh).
- `--liters <n>`: With --km: measured consumption.
- `--km <n>`: With --liters: measured consumption.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt fuel 450 --consumption 6.5 --price 1.85 --people 2
toolbelt fuel 300 --ev --consumption 17 --price 0.25 --round-trip
toolbelt fuel --liters 42 --km 700
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/fuel

### cooking

Kitchen conversions (cups, spoons, grams by ingredient), oven temperatures and recipe scaling.

```
toolbelt cooking <amount> <from> <to> [--ingredient id] | toolbelt cooking --temp <n> [--temp-unit c|f|gas] | toolbelt cooking --servings 4:6 [recipe] | toolbelt cooking --list
```

- `-i, --ingredient <id>`: Ingredient, for volume ↔ mass (see --list). Default: water.
- `--temp <n>`: Oven temperature to convert.
- `--temp-unit <c|f|gas>`: Unit of --temp. Default: c.
- `--servings <from:to>`: Scale the recipe (input) from this many servings to that many.
- `--factor <n>`: Scale the recipe (input) by this factor.
- `--decimal-comma`: Write scaled decimals with a comma.
- `--list`: List the units and ingredients.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt cooking 1 cup g --ingredient flour
toolbelt cooking --temp 180
toolbelt cooking --servings 4:6 --file recipe.txt
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/cooking

### grades

Weighted grade average (any scale, or German 1–6), percent, letter/GPA, and the grade needed next.

Aliases: `gpa`.

```
toolbelt grades "<grade>[/<out of>] [x<coef>]; ..." [--scale 20] [--target n --next-coef n] [--system scale|de]
```

- `--scale <n>`: Scale of the average (20, 10, 100…). Default: 20.
- `--system <scale|de>`: de: German grades 1 (best) to 6, with + and −. Default: scale.
- `--target <n>`: Target average: print the grade needed next.
- `--next-coef <n>`: Coefficient of the next grade. Default: 1.

One grade per line or separated by ";": "15", "15/20", "8/10 x2" (out of 10, coefficient 2).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt grades "15/20 x2; 12; 8/10 x3"
toolbelt grades "12; 9; 14" --target 12 --next-coef 2
toolbelt grades "2+; 3; 1-" --system de
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/grades

### eta

When will it be done: progress, pace and finish time; the pace needed for a deadline; time at a given pace.

```
toolbelt eta --total n --done n (--start <date> | --elapsed <hours>) [--deadline <date>] [--zone z] | toolbelt eta --left n --speed n [--per minute|hour|day]
```

- `--total <n>`: Total amount of work.
- `--done <n>`: Amount done so far.
- `--start <date>`: When it started (ISO date, read in --zone).
- `--elapsed <n>`: Hours since the start (instead of --start).
- `--deadline <date>`: Print the pace needed to finish by then.
- `--left <n>`: What is left (pace mode).
- `--speed <n>`: Items per --per (pace mode).
- `--per <minute|hour|day>`: Unit of --speed. Default: hour.
- `-z, --zone <zone>`: Time zone of dates. Default: UTC.

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt eta --total 120 --done 30 --elapsed 2
toolbelt eta --total 500 --done 120 --start 2026-01-15T08:00 --deadline 2030-12-31T18:00
toolbelt eta --left 90 --speed 20 --per hour
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/eta

### countdown

Time left until a date (days, hours, minutes), calendar days and working days left.

```
toolbelt countdown <YYYY-MM-DD[THH:mm] | MM-DD> [--holidays <dates>]
```

- `--holidays <dates>`: Days off to skip in the working days, comma-separated YYYY-MM-DD.

Dates are in local time. MM-DD means the next time that day comes (birthdays, holidays).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt countdown 2026-12-25
toolbelt countdown 2026-07-14T18:00 --json
toolbelt countdown 2026-05-31 --holidays "2026-05-01,2026-05-08,2026-05-14"
toolbelt countdown 12-25   # Next Christmas.
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/countdown

### random

Random numbers, dice (2d6+3), coin flips, pick winners, shuffle, teams and Secret Santa.

Aliases: `dice`.

```
toolbelt random [number] [--min <n>] [--max <n>] [--count <n>] [--decimals <n>] [--unique]
       toolbelt random dice <notation>      (or: toolbelt random 2d6+3)
       toolbelt random coin [--count <n>]
       toolbelt random shuffle|pick|teams|santa [items…] (else one per line from --file or stdin)
```

- `--min <n>`: Smallest number (number mode). Default: 1.
- `--max <n>`: Largest number (number mode). Default: 100.
- `-n, --count <n>`: How many numbers, flips or winners (pick). Default: 1.
- `--decimals <n>`: Decimal places (number mode). Default: 0.
- `--unique`: No repeated numbers.
- `--teams <n>`: Number of teams (teams mode). Default: 2.
- `--size <n>`: Team size instead of a number of teams (teams mode).
- `-x, --exclude <a,b | a>b>`: Secret Santa exclusion (repeatable): "Alice,Bob" both ways, "Alice>Bob" one way.
- `--seed <n>`: Seed for a reproducible draw (default: crypto randomness).

Examples:

```sh
toolbelt random --min 1 --max 6 --count 3
toolbelt random 4d6kh3+2   # Dice notation: keep the 3 highest of 4d6, plus 2.
toolbelt random coin --count 5
toolbelt random pick Alice Bob Carol Dave --count 2
toolbelt random teams --file names.txt --teams 3
toolbelt random santa Alice Bob Carol Dave --exclude "Alice,Bob"
```

Site: https://maxgfr.github.io/toolbelt/#/random
